title: Gospel Book
medium: Ink and opaque watercolor on parchment
source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Cloisters Collection and Director's Fund, 2015 (2015.560)
note: Seven canon-table pages of the same book, each cut by hand-read geometry and colour distance from the vellum into separate parts: one arch row (split at runtime into bays and ends), capitals, shafts and bases per column. Text and rubrics touching the parts removed; edge colour un-mixed from the vellum. Columns against the binding (the last shaft or base on folios 16, 18, 21, 24, and the last capital on 18, 21 and 24) are left out and replaced at runtime by a sister of the same colour; the right ends of 18, 21 and 24 are drawn as their own left end, mirrored. Sharpness checked with tools/engine inspect (all pass) and every part with alpha_check. Scripts: tools/engine/jobs/canon-tables-work/cut.py, pack.py.

title: Zeyt'un Gospels
medium: Tempera colors, gold leaf, and ink on parchment
source: J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles, Ms. 59 (95.MG.4)
note: All eight canon pages, each with two bays (fols. 1v-8: four facing openings), worked at 2100 px wide from the IIIF images (3168 x 4418; fol. 6 4600 x 6400). The bays (the old canon table, its gold ruling and headings) and the place of each column are refilled with parchment: tone from the bays' own bare parchment, grain tiled from the page's bottom margin with its strength matched. Each column (with its corbel and its red and gold flecks) is lifted off as a separate part with edge colour un-mixed from the parchment. Everything outside the bays is the photograph. All files pass the engine's inspect.
